correctness.rationale: For every n≥2 and 0<q≤1 each source-target infection has probability q^d if and only if the path times are increasing toward target. Summing ordered pairs yields mandatory distance-1 and distance-2 contributions and optional d≥3 contributions; all extrema and equality classes follow. Uniform permutations make exactly 2/d! of each distance-d unordered interval traversable. For q=1-1/n Riemann summation gives upper/n→e^{-1}, minimum→4 and random mean→2e−1. A separate exact-rational event-by-event verifier exhausts n≤7 and q=1/2,2/3,1 with 10,494 successful assertions; finite tests are not a proof of the all-n result.

originality.rationale: The investigated gap is the exact extremal uniformly seeded expected final SI outbreak on one-shot edge-ordered paths for all n and q, including equality orders and the divergence of maximum/minimum while direct index reproduction is fixed. Holme–Masuda studies epidemic prediction on empirical temporal networks rather than sharp path optimization; Enright–Meeks–Skerman optimize worst-source maximum temporal reachability, not the uniform-source expectation or stochastic q; the published injectively timed path result concerns multi-seed synchronous zero forcing, not this single-seed stochastic process. Full text was read for closest three. Factorial probabilities are pre-existing, and exhaustive priority is not claimed.

value.rationale: A motivated natural temporal-network question is fully solved: for one-shot path contacts, how does calendar ordering control expected epidemic final size under fixed graph, seed law and per-contact risk? The exact sharp all-n/q classification, random benchmark and unbounded max/min separation at identical direct index offspring mean offer a substantive structural boundary for reproduction-number-based outbreak predictions. No claim is made for realistic recurrent-contact or recovery dynamics.
